messages:
marta: quick heads up, canary out to ~5% landed ~10m ago, noticed a UI gap — some Viewer users still see the 'Edit' button on Project settings :eyes:
samir: thanks, can you repro and grab a screenshot and the user id?
marta: yep, repro on staging with user id uid: 9892. screenshot attached (ui shows edit button but backend denies on save)
alex: likely a frontend gating flag mismatch, we recently moved some checks to the permission matrix helper. rolling a quick check now.
kevin: backend logs show a 403 on the save call from uid 9892, but response body is generic. can you paste the request/response?
marta: request -> POST /api/projects/42/settings body {"name":"x"}
kevin: response -> 403 {"err":"forbidden","code":"perm_denied"} — so backend denies, frontend still shows button = client-side bug or cache.
samir: what bothers me: audit logs for UI clicks are generated by the frontend before the save call. we may have false-positive audit entries. need to ensure KMS/audit pipeline tags the event as 'ui-intent' vs 'server-allowed'
securitybot: new_audit_event id=evt_20260301_772 created for actor=9892 action=ui.click.edit_project project=42 stream=kms-ingest
alex: I think the permission helper uses a cached role mask from localStorage during async rehydrates. if the role changed server-side recently the cached mask can be stale. I'll add a synchronous server check before rendering edit affordances for sensitive routes.
samir: agree. short-term mitigation: hide edit button unless server says explicit allow (api: /api/projects/42/permissions -> {can_edit:true}). longer term: fix cache invalidation and add telemetry to measure occurrences.
marta: can you run a query for how many users hit UI edit affordance while server responded 403 in last 24h?
kevin: running quick SQL on events table:
```
SELECT count(1) FROM ui_events u
JOIN server_responses s ON u.request_id = s.request_id
WHERE u.event = 'click.edit_project' AND s.status = 403 AND s.route = '/api/projects/%';
```
kevin: results = 37 in the last 24h (mostly from canary cohort).
samir: 37 is non-trivial. we should treat as a medium vuln: misleading affordances and noisy audit. propose fixes: 1) frontend: server-validated gating on sensitive UIs 2) backend: upgrade audit event schema to include "server_outcome" and KMS signature of final action 3) rollout: kill canary and patch immediately 
alex: I'll push a small patch to check /permissions before showing button. pushing branch now.
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary=5% service=frontend commit=fd3a8b4
marta: I'll monitor canary traffic for misclicks and post metrics
securitybot: kms_log entry id=kms_20260301_889: audit schema update queued, needs migration PR (migration id 2026-03-audit-schema)
samir: created GH issue #4825 and assigned to @kevin for schema work and @alex for frontend. Kevin: can you add a migration plan for KMS-wrapped audit entries? include backwards compatibility for the analytic pipeline.
kevin: yes — plan: add new column server_outcome varchar, signature_id varchar; backfill script to tag existing events as 'unknown' outcome; ship in two-step deploy. will open PR today.
samir: also add a small unit test to ensure frontend doesn't render edit affordance if /permissions returns {can_edit:false} even if local cache says true.
alex: adding test now.
marta: after the patch, let's re-run the SQL to confirm drop back to ~0 errors before resuming canary.
samir: good plan. assigning incident severity P2 for tracking, notify on Slack if >10 occurrences after patch. :thumbsup:
kevin: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/5109
alex: frontend PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/5110
marta: thanks team — tagging this thread for postmortem notes and compliance report prep (we'll need to show KMS audit fix and mitigation steps).
securitybot: incident_log id=inc_2026_03_01_12 recorded severity=P2 owner=@samir
samir: I'll prepare a short blameless postmortem and a runbook update for permission cache invalidation.
marta: closing canary now until backend migration lands.
deploy-bot: deploy cancelled for canary=5% service=frontend commit=fd3a8b4
kevin: once migration merged we should rotate KMS signing keys in staging and verify audit pipeline signatures. I'll schedule a rotation window.
samir: ok, thanks all. follow-ups: GH #4825, PRs 5109/5110. will loop in compliance for evidence pack.
